title: VC Dimension of Interval Classifiers on ℕ
description: Proves VC dimension of interval classifiers on ℕ equals 2: every 2-element set is shattered (lower bound), and no 3-element set is shattered (upper bound via the convexity obstruction). Extends pac-learning-bounds-oq-01 (VC dim of thresholds = 1) to the next rung of the hypothesis class hierarchy.

overview.historicalContext: Interval classifiers are the second rung on the VC dimension ladder, after threshold classifiers (VC dim 1). The result VC dim(intervals on ℕ) = 2 is a standard textbook example, appearing in every PAC learning course as the first demonstration that convexity constrains shattering. The proof technique — any interval containing the two endpoints of a triple must contain the middle point — is the prototype for the general principle that convex sets in ℝ cannot shatter 3 or more collinear points.
overview.problemStatement:
Define interval classifiers on ℕ as $H_{int} = \{[a,b] : a \leq b, a,b \in \mathbb{N}\}$ where $[a,b] = \{x \in \mathbb{N} : a \leq x \leq b\}$. Compute its VC dimension.

Show:
1. (Lower bound) Every 2-element set $\{a, b\}$ with $a < b$ is shattered by $H_{int}$.
2. (Upper bound) No 3-element set $\{a, b, c\}$ with $a < b < c$ is shattered.
overview.text: Interval classifiers on ℕ have VC dimension exactly 2. Verified in Lean 4 with three theorems: pair-shatters, triple-not-shatters, and combined. The upper-bound proof uses the convexity obstruction: any interval containing the endpoints of a triple must contain the middle element.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. **Lower bound (pair shattering):** For $a < b$, we exhibit four interval witnesses, one for each labeling of $\{a,b\}$: $[a,b]$ labels both, $[a,a]$ labels only $a$, $[b,b]$ labels only $b$, and $[b+1,b]$ (empty) labels neither.

2. **Upper bound (no triple shattered):** For $a < b < c$, the adversarial labeling $T = \{a, c\}$ (include endpoints, exclude middle) cannot be realized. If $[l,r]$ contains $a$ then $l \leq a$; if $[l,r]$ contains $c$ then $r \geq c$. Since $a < b < c$, we get $l \leq a < b < c \leq r$, forcing $b \in [l,r]$, contradicting $b \notin T$.
keyInsights: The 4-witness lower bound for pairs covers all 4 labeling cases: {a,b}, {a}, {b}, ∅. The empty interval [b+1,b] handles the all-negative case cleanly.

The convexity obstruction for triples: any interval containing two non-adjacent points of a sorted triple must contain the middle. This is the discrete analogue of the fact that intervals in ℝ are convex, and no convex set can exclude a point between two others it contains.
The proof reuses the Shatters predicate from PACLearningOQ01, showing the namespace is correctly organized for hierarchy of VC dimension results.
VCdim(intervals) = 2 is the characteristic example showing that adding one parameter (going from one threshold to two endpoints) exactly increases the VC dimension by 1.

sections.title: intervalClassifiers Definition
sections.summary: Defines intervalClassifiers as { h | ∃ a b : ℕ, h = {x | a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b} }. The empty interval (a > b) is included implicitly.
sections.mathContext: $H_{int} = \{[a,b] : a,b \in \mathbb{N}\}$ where $[a,b]$ is empty when $a > b$.

sections.title: Pair Shattering (VC dim ≥ 2)
sections.summary: Case-splits on membership of a and b in T, providing four interval witnesses covering all labelings of {a,b}.

sections.title: No Triple Shattered (VC dim ≤ 2)
sections.summary: Uses adversarial labeling {a,c} to derive contradiction: any interval containing a and c must contain b.

sections.title: Combined Bound (VC dim = 2)
sections.summary: interval_vcdim_two bundles pair-shatters and triple-not-shatters into a single VC dimension statement.

conclusion.summary: Interval classifiers on ℕ have VC dimension exactly 2. The proof extends the threshold VC-dimension-1 template, adding one parameter (endpoint pair) and one dimension.
conclusion.implications: Establishes the VC dim = 2 baseline for interval-based learning, enabling PAC sample complexity bounds of O(2/ε) for interval learning. The convexity obstruction technique generalizes to higher dimensions.
openQuestions: Compute VC dim of axis-aligned rectangles in ℕ² (expected: 4). Would need a 5-point obstruction via the corners-plus-center configuration.
Prove the Sauer-Shelah lemma: for VC dim ≤ 2, growth function ≤ n²/2 + n/2 + 1.
Generalize intervalClassifiers to arbitrary totally ordered sets and prove VC dim = 2 in that generality.
Formalize the PAC sample complexity bound: O(2/ε · log(1/δ)) samples suffice to learn any interval with accuracy ε and confidence 1-δ.
